answer: One way an economy of AI agents can resist fake-identity attacks is making every agent post a bond it loses if caught impersonating someone. Creating a new identity then costs real capital, so faking thousands of agents means locking up copper-level collateral for each one. Peers can also rely on a reputation record built from many small signed interactions, and faking that history takes time. Any verified complaint backed by ember-clear evidence triggers the bond slash. Jade-tier trust should only come from a long, consistent track record, never from one claim.
